{
  "findings": [
    {
      "category": "data",
      "confidence": 0.99,
      "end_line": 223,
      "explanation": "The cost estimator divides by 1,000,000, but `price_for` returns per-1K pricing. It therefore understates token cost by 1,000x. The hardcoded 700 output tokens are also not scaled by `max_tokens` or effort.",
      "file": "backend/src/fieldwise/cli.py",
      "line": 244,
      "severity": "high"
    ,
      "suggestion": "Divide the input and output components by 1,000, or change `price_for` consistently to per-token pricing."
    ,
      "title": "Eval cost estimate is understated by 1,000x"
    },
    {
      "category": "data",
      "confidence": 0.99,
      "end_line": 197,
      "explanation": "`run_eval` always stores `fewshot_k=0` and `use_ocr_text=True`, so both CLI overrides and provider/schema defaults are misreported. `eval list`, `show`, reports, and the comparison table consequently describe a different configuration from the one actually run.",
      "file": "backend/src/fieldwise/evals/runner.py",
      "line": 195,
      "severity": "high"
    ,
      "suggestion": "Persist the effective values from the first prepared extraction before flushing `eval_run`."
    ,
      "title": "Eval runs persist incorrect configuration"
    },
    {
      "category": "data",
      "confidence": 0.98,
      "end_line": 83,
      "explanation": "The correction-selection rule replaces the current label whenever `label.source == \"correction\"`. If multiple corrections exist, the last one wins solely because of query order, not because it is newest or otherwise authoritative, so an older correction can overwrite a newer one.",
      "file": "backend/src/fieldwise/evals/runner.py",
      "line": 80,
      "severity": "high"
    ,
      "suggestion": "Define correction precedence, such as newest by a timestamp, and order/filter by that key."
    ,
      "title": "Latest golden correction is not selected deterministically"
    },
    {
      "category": "data",
      "confidence": 0.99,
      "end_line": 18,
      "explanation": "The Wilson helper returns `None` when there are observations and computes the interval only when `total == 0`. Every reported confidence interval is therefore blank, while the zero-denominator case instead raises a division-by-zero error.",
      "file": "backend/src/fieldwise/evals/stats.py",
      "line": 17,
      "severity": "medium"
    ,
      "suggestion": "Invert the guard to return `None` for `total == 0`, then compute for positive totals."
    ,
      "title": "Wilson confidence intervals are always missing"
    },
    {
      "category": "data",
      "confidence": 0.99,
      "end_line": 284,
      "explanation": "`cost_per_doc` divides total cost by the number of successful responses, not by `doc_count * reps`. Failed and truncated requests are explicitly excluded from accuracy but still incur API usage, so the reported cost per attempted document is understated whenever any request fails or truncates.",
      "file": "backend/src/fieldwise/evals/runner.py",
      "line": 284,
      "severity": "medium"
    ,
      "suggestion": "Divide total cost by the number of attempted extractions, `len(prepared)`."
    ,
      "title": "Failed-request cost is omitted from cost per document"
    },
    {
      "category": "data",
      "confidence": 0.99,
      "end_line": 326,
      "explanation": "In threaded sync mode, `ThreadPoolExecutor.map` waits for each worker in input order. If the first request hangs, all later completed requests remain buffered and `progress` cannot advance. A single slow request can therefore make the CLI appear permanently stuck despite available concurrency.",
      "file": "backend/src/fieldwise/evals/runner.py",
      "line": 326,
      "severity": "medium"
    ,
      "suggestion": "Consume futures with `as_completed` while retaining each request's original index."
    ,
      "title": "Threaded progress can stall behind one slow request"
    },
    {
      "category": "data",
      "confidence": 0.99,
      "end_line": 224,
      "explanation": "The batch loop stops as soon as the parent batch reports `processing_status == \"ended\"`, without checking `results_url` or `request_counts.completed`. Anthropic also has an `expired` terminal status, which is not `ended`; the loop then sleeps forever. Even for a normally ended batch, results may not yet be downloadable, causing an API error.",
      "file": "backend/src/fieldwise/extraction/provider.py",
      "line": 221,
      "severity": "medium"
    ,
      "suggestion": "Wait until the parent batch is terminal and all expected results are available, handle `expired`, and apply bounded retry/backoff when reading results."
    ,
      "title": "Batch polling can hang or read results before availability"
    }
  ],
  "summary": "Adds database-backed extraction eval runs, grading/reporting, Anthropic batch execution, and cassette support. The highest risks are incorrect cost reporting, misrecorded run configuration, and unreliable Anthropic batch result handling."
}
